title: Déjeuner sur le bateau  (Lunch on the Boat)

segments.t: At the Cannes luxury hotel, powerful media mogul Jean-Denis Gillieres corners Andrea, insisting on meeting with Juliette Binoche. Learning that Juliette despises his advances, Andrea cleverly arranges a business lunch on his private yacht for a day when Juliette will have already left town. Listen to the scene in French first.
Juliette, je suis avec Jean-Denis Gillières.
Il veut te voir tout de suite.
Non, je t'en supplie, pas lui!
Je ne veux pas le voir.
Il est tellement pénible!
Il ne comprend pas le mot non.
D'accord, je m'en occupe.
Juliette est vraiment désolée, monsieur.
Elle répète son discours important.
J'adore les femmes intelligentes!
Elle prépare son premier film.
Déjeunons sur mon bateau, lundi.
Ce sera calme et très agréable.
Je peux aider pour le financement.
Lundi, c'est parfait pour nous!
Let's walk through the conversation step by step.
Juliette, je suis avec Jean-Denis Gillières.
'Juliette, I am with Jean-Denis Gillieres.' Simple 'I am with' works identically in French and English when briefing someone discreetly over the phone.
Il veut te voir tout de suite.
'He wants to see you right away.' Casual 'you' sits ahead of 'to see' in French, followed by that handy three-word idiom meaning 'right away.'
Non, je t'en supplie, pas lui!
'No, I beg you, not him!' Literally 'I beg you of it,' that dramatic plea in French slips a tiny 'of it' stand-in right before 'beg.'
Je ne veux pas le voir.
'I do not want to see him.' Notice how 'not' wraps ONLY around 'want' in French, leaving 'him to see' untouched afterward.
Il est tellement pénible!
'He is so tiresome!' That final description comes from 'pain' or 'trouble,' making it the go-to French insult for someone exhausting and pushy.
Il ne comprend pas le mot non.
'He does not understand the word no.' Saying 'the word no' word for word gives Juliette's complaint crystal-clear punch in French.
D'accord, je m'en occupe.
'Understood, I am taking care of it.' Literally 'I occupy myself of it,' this reassuring handy sentence tells someone 'leave it to me!'
Juliette est vraiment désolée, monsieur.
'Juliette is truly sorry, sir.' Notice how Andrea pivots from casual 'you' on the phone to formal 'sir' the second she faces Gillieres.
Elle répète son discours important.
'She is rehearsing her important speech.' Fun double life: the action here means both 'repeat' and 'rehearse' in French—since rehearsing is repeating lines!
J'adore les femmes intelligentes!
'I adore intelligent women!' Unlike English, which drops 'the' for general groups, French requires 'the women intelligent' even when speaking broadly.
Elle prépare son premier film.
'She is preparing her first film.' Ordinal 'first' is one of the select descriptions that sit BEFORE 'film' in French rather than after it.
Déjeunons sur mon bateau, lundi.
'Let us have lunch on my boat on Monday.' Dropping 'we' turns the first-person plural ending directly into 'let's have lunch,' and days like 'Monday' need no 'on' in French.
Ce sera calme et très agréable.
'It will be calm and very pleasant.' Future-tense 'that will be' pairs two easy descriptions—with the second being a direct cognate of 'agreeable.'
Je peux aider pour le financement.
'I can help with the financing.' Where English says 'help with,' French links 'help' to 'the financing' using 'for.'
Lundi, c'est parfait pour nous!

'Monday is perfect for us!' Naming 'Monday' first and following up with 'that is perfect' is a classic conversational topic-comment pattern in French. Now let's listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.
Juliette, je suis avec Jean-Denis Gillières.
Il veut te voir tout de suite.
Non, je t'en supplie, pas lui!
Je ne veux pas le voir.
Il est tellement pénible!
Il ne comprend pas le mot non.
D'accord, je m'en occupe.
Juliette est vraiment désolée, monsieur.
Elle répète son discours important.
J'adore les femmes intelligentes!
Elle prépare son premier film.
Déjeunons sur mon bateau, lundi.
Ce sera calme et très agréable.
Je peux aider pour le financement.
Lundi, c'est parfait pour nous!
By agreeing to a yacht lunch after Juliette's departure, Andrea protects her star client while politely humoring the wealthy mogul. See you next time!
Au revoir!
